usage.reason: The user record has no last-active or last-login field. The only activity-style source is the audit records endpoint, which logs administrative configuration changes (identified by authorKey), not product usage, so it cannot show who actually uses Jira.

evidence.quote: Returns a list of all users, including active users, inactive users and previously deleted users that have an Atlassian account.
You can access this resource via basic auth.

assumptions: The source does not state the maximum page size for the user list; 100 is a sensible guess.
The user list returns a bare JSON array, so recordsPath is written as '$' (the top-level array). Confirm the runtime accepts this.
Pagination uses startAt and maxResults; the source does not say when the last page is reached, so the runtime should stop on an empty or short page.
Because the user list is an offset-based endpoint, the runtime must stop when a page returns no rows.
Email addresses may be hidden by users' privacy settings, so some emails may be blank.
The source does not list the read:jira-user scope in its truncated scope list, but the endpoints state it as required.

OAuth 2.0 (3LO) calls normally go through api.atlassian.com with a cloud ID, which the source does not describe; the base URL here is the site's own host. Basic auth with an API token is the confirmed route against that host.
Basic auth uses a person's API token, so access stops if that person leaves; no service-account or client-credentials method is documented.
Usage is marked unavailable: no per-user last-active field exists and the audit log only records admin configuration changes, and requires the manage:jira-configuration scope.
The source says nothing about rate limits, so those fields are left empty.
Users with account type 'customer' are assumed to be guests (e.g. service desk customers).
